description: Hazard colouring (ForeFlight's Hazard Advisor): the ground and obstacles on the map against the altitude flown, the GPS's in flight (`underway`, flying speed), the plan's cruise on the ground. Red over `warning_from_ft`, the altitude less the pilot's clearance -- 500 ft (14 CFR 91.119(c)), 1,000 ft by default (91.119(b), 91.177(a)(2)(ii)) or 2,000 ft (91.177(a)(2)(i), a Part 95 mountainous area); exactly the clearance meets the rule and is yellow -- yellow from `caution_from_ft`, 1,000 ft under that, nothing below. `shown` where the setting (off, on, or by itself in flight) and an altitude allow; each of `tops_ft` (obstacle tops, ft MSL) as `levels` against the bands ("warning", "caution", "clear"; null with no altitude). A picture against one altitude, not terrain clearance: no TAWS (TSO-C151). A phone's GPS height is over the WGS84 ellipsoid, some 100 ft under sea level over the US (GEOID18), so it errs red.

setting.description: The Map card's Hazard Colouring: off, on, or on by itself in flight.

speed_kt.description: The GPS's ground speed, kt; null with no fix.

gps_altitude_ft.description: The GPS's height, ft, where it gives one.

clearance_ft.description: The pilot's clearance, one of clearances_ft; the default for null or another.

tops_ft.description: Obstacle tops, ft MSL, to colour.
